explanation: Not on the erdosproblems.com/875 page itself; compared against the abstract of Erdős–Nicolas–Sárközy, 'Sommes de sous-ensembles' (Numdam JTNB_1991__3_1_55_0): 'Finally, we construct an infinite admissible set A such that A(x) = Card{a ∈ A; a ≤ x} ≫ x^{5−2√6}', where admissible means subsets of different cardinalities have different sums. The Lean statement: ∃ infinite admissible A and c > 0 with c·x^{5−2√6} ≤ countingFunction A x for all large x. The definitions of admissibility agree (for sets of positive integers) and ≫ is unpacked correctly. Faithful.
